critic_risk_flags: Despite semantic appeal (explicit H), SEIHR adds hospitalization transition/dwell parameters that are likely weakly identifiable in a short single-season series; surveillance risk note flags this explicitly. This raises over-complexity/instability risk relative to delayed_I mappings that already match the target timing.

I+H further compounds identifiability and interpretability issues: mixing states can blur what the hospitalization-rate target represents (admissions vs census vs proxy), and with limited data it can create non-identifiable tradeoffs between I and H amplitudes/durations. Not clearly justified given recommended delayed_I and the short series length.
